questions.q: Why does a CI pipeline run tests automatically instead of relying on developers to run them locally first?
options: Local test runs are always slower than CI
It removes the need to trust that someone remembered to run them, and makes the proof visible to everyone
pytest cannot run on a developer's own laptop
CI runners have more test cases than local machines
questions.explain: Running tests in the pipeline turns 'did you test this' from a trust-based question into a visible, automatic check attached to the commit itself.

questions.q: In the test pyramid, why should a pipeline run unit tests before end-to-end tests?
options: End-to-end tests are not allowed to run in CI
Unit tests are slower and should be saved for last
Unit tests are fast and cheap; failing fast on them avoids wasting time on a slow E2E run that was always going to fail
GitHub Actions requires alphabetical step ordering
questions.explain: Running cheap, fast tests first lets the pipeline fail fast, giving a quick answer instead of waiting for an expensive end-to-end run doomed by the same underlying bug.

questions.q: How does a GitHub Actions step actually determine whether `pytest tests/unit` passed or failed?
options: GitHub Actions parses the English text of the test output
By the exit code the pytest command returns — zero for success, non-zero for failure
By checking whether the file tests/unit still exists afterward
A human must manually mark the step green or red
questions.explain: Workflow engines react to a command's exit code, not its printed output. pytest exits 0 only when every test passes.

questions.q: What does the `--maxfail=1` flag do in `pytest tests/unit --maxfail=1`?
options: Limits the test suite to one test total
Stops the test run at the first failure instead of running every remaining test
Retries a failing test up to one more time
Sets a one-minute timeout on the whole job
questions.explain: --maxfail=1 halts the suite as soon as one test fails, avoiding a long run through many tests likely failing for the same root cause.

questions.q: On a GitHub pull request, where can a reviewer see the combined pass/fail result of every job from every workflow at a glance?
options: The repository's README
The Checks tab
The commit's email notification only
There is no combined view; each workflow must be checked separately
questions.explain: The Checks tab on a pull request rolls up every job from every triggered workflow into one summary view.
